entities.summary: Qifu Guoren, also known by his posthumous name as the Prince Xuanlie of Western Qin (西秦宣烈王), was the founding monarch of the Xianbei-led Western Qin dynasty of China. Born around 350 CE, Qifu Guoren ascended to the throne in 384 CE after the death of his father, Qifu Jun. He played a crucial role in the unification of the region by defeating the various warlords and establishing a strong foundation for the dynasty. His reign marked the beginning of a new era in Western Qin, characterized by military campaigns, administrative reforms, and cultural achievements. Qifu Guoren's legacy extended beyond his own time, as his successors continued to build upon his foundations, shaping the course of Chinese history. He was buried in the city of Pingcheng, capital of the Western Qin dynasty, where his tomb remains a testament to his enduring impact. The prince's military campaigns expanded the dynasty's borders, incorporating the territories of modern-day Gansu and Ningxia. He also promoted the development of trade and commerce, establishing new roads and communication networks that facilitated the exchange of goods and ideas. Qifu Guoren's reign is often seen as a pivotal moment in the history of Western Qin, marking the transition from a fragmented and chaotic region to a unified and prosperous state. His name is still remembered today as a symbol of courage, wisdom, and leadership. Despite the passage of centuries, Qifu Guoren's legacy continues to inspire historical study and admiration.
